chunk_map.heading: A signal that can only say yes is not a test
Agents shrink "can we build it?"; two questions remain
Test first what matters most and is proven least

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: S2 l.12: "the post-its that matter most" is the nearest to unresolved, but "map your bet" in the same sentence and "assumption map" at l.4 supply the antecedent; S1 l.10 "He"/"His" -> Barry O'Reilly l.4; S2 l.10 "the third one" -> Feasible l.8, same chunk. Harm (reader cannot resolve a referent) absent.

grep for "lecture|exercise|module|earlier|previous|above|below" in the three bodies -> 0 hits; closest S2 l.12 "when you map your bet" points forward to an exercise by action, not by file position, and names no file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no "the X you did/saw/caught" backward reference in any body

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no guess-before-reveal or live-demo beat in any body

rules_evaluated.evidence: S1 l.4-12, S2 l.4-12, S3 l.4-8 each carry a self-contained claim; shortest, S3, states the rule plus Bland quote plus the agent/team split.

S2 l.1 header "Agents shrink \"can we build it?\"; two questions remain" vs l.10 "Agents make much of the third one cheap... The first two they cannot settle" -> consistent; S1 l.1 and S3 l.1 likewise summarise their bodies.

grep -c "Not .*\. Not " over the three bodies -> 0; closest S3 l.4 "that customers want it, that the business should do it, that the team can build it" is a triple but each leg is concrete and distinct; S3 l.6 "much more valuable than the map itself" is an attributed Bland quote, not a self-grading superlative.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -ciE "compendium|forcing function|beat|mood|firing|writing surface" over the three bodies (above the maintainer cut) -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: S1 l.6-8 bolds the three template line-openers (**We believe**, **will result in**, **We will have confidence to proceed when**); the third is 7 words, above the ~5 cap, but these are the checklist item names of one three-line template, and the fidelity guard keeps O'Reilly's wording; S2 and S3 bodies carry 0 bold. Harm (monoculture of bolded lead sentences) absent. Non-blocking either way.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/lectures/apt101-write-the-bet.md -> "slides: 3 ... oversized: 0", the three include-links at lecture l.3,5,7 each resolve to curriculum/slides/<id>.md.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no Phase/Step headers or hand-numbered headers; node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js -> OK

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/lectures/apt101-write-the-bet.md -> "OK — 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut."

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no in-body links in any slide body

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/lectures/apt101-write-the-bet.md -> exit 0, "oversized: 0" (limits 210 words / 6 bullets); max bullets on any slide is 3.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: lecture headings are claims: S1 l.1 "A signal that can only say yes is not a test", S2 l.1 "Agents shrink ... two questions remain", S3 l.1 "Test first what matters most and is proven least" (closest to a label, an imperative law, still a claim).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: S3 l.4 "The unimportant ones can wait." is the closest to class (a) doctrine restatement of the header; it adds the converse priority, one short clause, and the sentence carries the Bland quote. S1 l.12 closer is a move, not a koan restating the header. Cut offered as suggestion only.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: S1 header came from the body's former closing line (maintainer block) and l.4-12 answer it; S2 was rewritten with its header the same day, l.4-12 answer it; S3 l.1 header is answered by l.4. No inherited bullets answering an old header.

suggestions.now: So when you map your bet, the post-its that matter most are the ones about wanting and should.
suggestions.proposed: So when you map your bet, the assumptions that matter most are the ones about wanting and should.

suggestions.now: Test first the ones that matter most and have the least evidence, "important and unproven" in David Bland's words. The unimportant ones can wait.
suggestions.proposed: Test first the ones that matter most and have the least evidence, "important and unproven" in David Bland's words.
